skills.title: Apply index laws for positive, zero, negative, and fractional exponents

cpa.concrete: Base-10 blocks and physical place-value disks. Repeatedly grouping/ungrouping stacks of 10 demonstrates positive power growth (10¹, 10², 10³) and division partitioning (10⁻¹, 10⁻², 10⁻³).
cpa.pictorial: Exponential number lines and shifting place-value charts. Show multiplication by 10ⁿ as shifting the decimal place or digit positions on a visual grid.
cpa.abstract: Index rules: $a^m \cdot a^n = a^{m+n}$, $\frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}$, $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$, $a^0 = 1$, $a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}$, $a^{1/n} = \sqrt[n]{a}$. Scientific notation $A \times 10^n$.

misconceptions.description: Student multiplies bases together ($2^5 \cdot 2^{-2} = 4^3$) instead of keeping base 2.
misconceptions.probe: Look at the numerator first: what index law applies when multiplying identical bases ($2^5 \cdot 2^{-2}$)?
misconceptions.correction: Apply the product rule $2^{5+(-2)} = 2^3$, then apply quotient rule $2^{3-7} = 2^{-4} = \frac{1}{2^4} = \frac{1}{16}$.

misconceptions.description: Adding coefficients directly without matching powers ($4.8 + 7.6 = 12.4 \times 10^9$).
misconceptions.probe: Can you add numbers directly when their powers of 10 differ? Think of adding 480,000 + 76,000.

cpa.concrete: Two-pan balance scales with labeled cups (variables x and y) and unit gram weights. Physically replacing one cup with equivalent cups/weights demonstrates substitution.
cpa.pictorial: Singapore comparison bar models. Draw proportional rectangular bars representing x and y to show how totals compare and reveal the replacement value of a variable block.
cpa.abstract: Simultaneous systems $ax + by = c$, substitution method, elimination method, and graphical intersection point $(x, y)$.

formulas: \text{Elimination: Multiply by factors to align coefficients}

misconceptions.description: Forgetting to distribute the factor of 2 to all terms: writing $3x + 4x + 1 = 16$ instead of $3x + 4x + 2 = 16$.
misconceptions.probe: Equation (1) tells you exactly what $y$ equals in terms of $x$. Where can you place that in the second equation?

misconceptions.description: Subtracting only the left sides and forgetting to subtract constants on the right (104 - 48).
misconceptions.probe: Assign variables to unknown quantities: $a =$ adult cost, $c =$ child cost.
misconceptions.correction: Multiply eq (2) by 2: $10a + 4c = 104$. Subtract eq (1): $7a = 56 \implies a = 8$. Back-substitute: $c = 6$.

skills.title: Expand products of algebraic expressions using Distributive Law

cpa.concrete: Physical algebra tiles ($x^2$ squares, $x$ rectangles, and 1-unit tiles) to build rectangular composite arrays. The dimensions represent factors; the total surface area represents the expanded polynomial.
cpa.pictorial: Geometric Area Models / 2x2 Grid Boxes showing $(a+b)(c+d) = ac + ad + bc + bd$.

misconceptions.description: Writing $(3x)^2$ as $3x^2$ by forgetting to square the coefficient 3.
misconceptions.probe: Look at the two sets of parentheses: identical terms with alternating signs (+ and -).
misconceptions.correction: Recognize form $(a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2$ where $a = 3x, b = 4$. $(3x)^2 - 4^2 = 9x^2 - 16$.

misconceptions.description: Attempting to factor $x^2 - y^2$ first as $(x-y)(x+y)$ and getting stuck with remaining $+6x+9$.
misconceptions.probe: Can you group three terms together that form a perfect square trinomial?
misconceptions.correction: $A^2 - B^2 = (A+B)(A-B)$ where $A = (x+3)$ and $B = y$. Gives $(x + y + 3)(x - y + 3)$.

skills.title: Factorize quadratic trinomials $ax^2 + bx + c$ using cross-multiplication and area methods

cpa.concrete: Use algebra tiles with positive and negative representations. Students arrange $x^2$ tiles, $x$ bars, and unit squares into complete rectangles. If a gap remains, zero pairs are introduced.
cpa.pictorial: Singapore Cross-Multiplication Frame (X-Method / Grid Box): diagonal multiplication and vertical sum check.
cpa.abstract: Standard form $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$. Zero Product Property: if $A \cdot B = 0$, then $A = 0$ or $B = 0$.

formulas: \text{Zero Product Property: } AB = 0 \implies A = 0 \text{ or } B = 0

misconceptions.description: Stopping at $(x - 3)(x - 4)$ without solving for the actual root values of $x$.
misconceptions.probe: What two numbers multiply to $+12$ and add up to $-7$?

misconceptions.description: Keeping $w = -5$ as a valid dimension in a physical real-world problem.
misconceptions.probe: Write an expression for length in terms of $w$: $\text{Length} = 2w + 3$.
misconceptions.correction: Factors of $2 \times (-35) = -70$ adding to $+3$ are $+10, -7$. $(2w - 7)(w + 5) = 0 \implies w = 3.5\text{ m}, \text{Length} = 10\text{ m}$. Reject $w = -5$.

cpa.concrete: Fraction equivalence strips and segmented rods to demonstrate why fractions cannot be combined without a shared denominator.
cpa.pictorial: Partitioned Area / Tape Diagrams. Visually partition fractional blocks into smaller identical grid units to model finding the Lowest Common Denominator (LCD).
cpa.abstract: Rational simplification $\frac{A \cdot C}{B \cdot C} = \frac{A}{B}$, common denominator $\frac{A}{B} \pm \frac{C}{D} = \frac{AD \pm BC}{BD}$, and checking undefined denominator values.

misconceptions.description: Cancelling individual terms like $x^2$ across addition/subtraction signs.
misconceptions.probe: Do not cancel individual terms like $x^2$ directly! Always factorize completely first.

misconceptions.description: Distributing $-2(x-2)$ as $-2x - 4$ instead of $-2x + 4$.
misconceptions.probe: Factor the denominator on the right-hand side first: $x^2 - x - 2 = (x - 2)(x + 1)$.

skills.title: Identify and establish congruence in triangles using formal tests (SSS, SAS, AAS/ASA, RHS)

cpa.concrete: Use Miras (reflective transparent panels), tracing paper (patty paper), and geoboards. Physically flipping tracing paper over a mirror line demonstrates congruence and line-of-reflection invariance.
cpa.pictorial: Coordinate Grid Ray Mappings. Draw perpendicular dashed guide lines from pre-image vertices to the mirror line and extend them an equal distance to plot the image points.
cpa.abstract: Congruence criteria: SSS, SAS, AAS/ASA, RHS. Reflection rules: over x-axis $(x, -y)$, y-axis $(-x, y)$, line $y = x \implies (y, x)$.

formulas: \triangle ABC \cong \triangle PQR \iff \text{All corresponding sides & angles equal}

misconceptions.description: Claiming congruence by ASS or SSA when the angle is not between the two known sides.
misconceptions.probe: List out the three pairs of equal parts given in the problem statement.
misconceptions.correction: Side $AB = PQ = 6$, Included $\angle B = \angle Q = 45^\circ$, Side $BC = QR = 8$. Conclude $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle PQR$ by SAS.

misconceptions.description: Negating coordinates instead of swapping them (confusing reflection across $y = x$ with axes).
misconceptions.probe: When a point reflects over the diagonal line $y = x$, what happens to $x$ and $y$?

skills.title: Apply angle properties of parallel lines intersected by transversals (F, Z, C angles)

cpa.concrete: Dynamic angle rotators and paper polygon cutouts. Tearing the three vertices off a paper triangle and lining them up on a straight edge proves the 180° interior sum tangibly.
cpa.pictorial: Geometric Transversal Highlight Diagrams. Highlight F, Z, and C shapes over complex figures to isolate parallel relationships.
cpa.abstract: Corresponding angles (equal, F), Alternate interior angles (equal, Z), Interior angles (supplementary, C, sum to 180°). Polygon interior sum $S_n = (n-2) \times 180^\circ$, exterior sum $= 360^\circ$.

misconceptions.description: Adding the expressions to equal $180^\circ$ by confusing alternate angles with consecutive interior angles.
misconceptions.probe: Look at the positions of $\angle APQ$ and $\angle PQD$. Do they form a Z-shape between the parallel lines?

misconceptions.description: Setting up a complex equation using the interior sum formula $\frac{(n-2)180}{n} = 5 \times 360$ and making algebraic mistakes.
misconceptions.probe: What is the sum of an interior angle and its adjacent exterior angle at any vertex?
misconceptions.correction: $5e + e = 180^\circ \implies 6e = 180^\circ \implies e = 30^\circ$. Number of sides $n = \frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ} = 12\text{ sides}$.

skills.title: Graph linear functions using gradient-intercept methods ($y = mx + c$)

cpa.concrete: Coordinate dry-erase grid mats and pegboards with color-coded rubber bands. Stretch bands to construct right-angled slope triangles along plotted lines.
cpa.pictorial: Value Tables & Step-Wise Rate-of-Change Diagrams. Draw step ladders on cartesian graphs to visually map unit horizontal steps against vertical increments (Δy).
cpa.abstract: Gradient $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}}$, $y = mx + c$. Parabola $a > 0$ opens upward (min), $a < 0$ opens downward (max). Axis of symmetry $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$.

misconceptions.description: Stating the gradient is $-3$ directly from $3x + 2y = 8$ without dividing by the coefficient 2.
misconceptions.probe: Isolate $y$ on one side of the equation to put it in $y = mx + c$ form.

misconceptions.description: Calculating $-(2)^2$ as $(-2)^2 = +4$ leading to $y = 17$ instead of $-4 + 8 + 5 = 9$.
misconceptions.probe: Look at the sign of the $x^2$ term ($a = -1$). Does it open up or down?

skills.title: Construct and interpret distance-time and speed-time graphs

cpa.concrete: Stopwatches, rolling toys, and measuring tape along a track. Students record distances at 2-second intervals to link physical movement directly with data tables.
cpa.pictorial: Segmented Line Profiles with slope annotations. Color code sections (e.g., steep red = fast, shallow blue = slow, flat green = stopped). Trapezoid area shading under speed curves.
cpa.abstract: Distance-Time gradient = Speed. Speed-Time gradient = Acceleration. Area under speed-time graph = Total distance traveled.

misconceptions.description: Forgetting to include the 30-minute rest period in the total elapsed time.
misconceptions.probe: For stage 1, use $\text{Speed} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}}$.
misconceptions.correction:
a) $\text{Speed}_1 = \frac{30}{1.5} = 20\text{ km/h}$.
b) $\text{Total Distance} = 50\text{ km}$, $\text{Total Time} = 1.5 + 0.5 + 1.0 = 3.0\text{ h}$. $\text{Avg Speed} = \frac{50}{3} = 16\frac{2}{3}\text{ km/h}$.

misconceptions.description: Using $d = s \times t = 24 \times 24 = 576\text{ m}$ assuming speed was constant throughout the whole trip.
misconceptions.probe: Acceleration is the gradient of the speed-time graph during the first 8 seconds: $\frac{v-u}{t}$.

skills.title: State and prove the Pythagorean Theorem ($a^2 + b^2 = c^2$)

cpa.concrete: Unit Square Grid Tile Puzzles. Arrange square sets of tiles (3×3=9 and 4×4=16) along the legs of a right triangle, then rearrange all 25 tiles to build a single 5×5=25 square along the hypotenuse.
cpa.pictorial: Geometric Proof Squares attached to triangle borders. 3D cuboid box diagonals broken into base right triangle + vertical height triangle.
cpa.abstract: In right triangle with hypotenuse $c$: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$. 3D space diagonal $D = \sqrt{l^2 + w^2 + h^2}$. Triples: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), (7,24,25).

misconceptions.description: Adding squares instead of subtracting ($13^2 + 5^2 = 194$), making the leg longer than the hypotenuse.
misconceptions.probe: Which side is the hypotenuse? Make sure 13 is isolated on the $c^2$ side of the equation.

misconceptions.description: Attempting to find the diagonal using only two dimensions ($8\text{ cm}$ and $24\text{ cm}$) without the width.
misconceptions.probe: Break this into two steps: first find the diagonal across the bottom floor of the box.

skills.title: Calculate the length and midpoint of a line segment using coordinates

cpa.concrete: Pegboards and coordinate grid boards with rubber bands. Students build right-angled slope triangles on the grid to see horizontal distance Δx and vertical distance Δy as triangle legs.
cpa.pictorial: Coordinate plane slope diagrams with labeled horizontal (Δx) and vertical (Δy) steps.
cpa.abstract: Distance $d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$, Midpoint $M = \left(\frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right)$, Gradient $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$, Perpendicular $m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1}$.

misconceptions.description: Calculating $4 - (-2)$ as 2 due to mishandling double negatives.
misconceptions.probe: For midpoint, take the average of the $x$-coordinates and average of the $y$-coordinates.

misconceptions.description: Using the original slope $m = 2$ instead of the negative reciprocal $m_\perp = -\frac{1}{2}$.
misconceptions.probe: A perpendicular bisector does two things: passes through the midpoint and meets at $90^\circ$.
misconceptions.correction: Midpoint $M = (4, 3)$. Slope $m_{AB} = \frac{7 - (-1)}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2$. Perpendicular slope $m_\perp = -\frac{1}{2}$. Line: $y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4) \implies y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5$.

cpa.concrete: Pegboards and coordinate grid boards with rubber bands. Students build right-angled slope triangles on the grid to see horizontal distance Δx and vertical distance Δy as triangle legs.
cpa.pictorial: Coordinate plane slope diagrams with labeled horizontal (Δx) and vertical (Δy) steps.
cpa.abstract: Distance $d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$, Midpoint $M = \left(\frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right)$, Gradient $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$, Perpendicular $m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1}$.

skills.title: Calculate surface areas and volumes of right pyramids, cylinders, cones, and spheres

cpa.concrete: Hollow geometric solids and water/sand pouring. Pouring 3 full cones of sand into an identical-radius cylinder confirms the 1/3 volume factor tangibly.
cpa.pictorial: Unfolded 2D Surface Nets. Draw the unrolled sector net of a cone and rectangular curved-face net of a cylinder to connect surface area formulas directly to 2D shapes.
cpa.abstract: Cylinder: $V = \pi r^2 h, TSA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2$. Cone: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h, CSA = \pi rl, l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}$. Sphere: $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3, SA = 4\pi r^2$. Solid hemisphere $TSA = 3\pi r^2$.

misconceptions.description: Using vertical height ($12\text{ cm}$) instead of slant height ($13\text{ cm}$) in the curved surface area formula.
misconceptions.probe: For volume, use $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$ with $r = 5$ and $h = 12$.
misconceptions.correction:
a) $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi (5^2)(12) = 100\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
b) Slant height $l = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13\text{ cm}$. $\text{TSA} = \pi rl + \pi r^2 = \pi(5)(13) + \pi(5^2) = 65\pi + 25\pi = 90\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

misconceptions.description: Adding the flat top circle of the cylinder and base of the hemisphere into the exterior surface area.
misconceptions.probe: Break the solid into its two components: bottom cylinder and top hemisphere.

skills.title: Calculate and interpret measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and spread (range, IQR)

cpa.concrete: Physical counting cubes, sorted length strips, and tactile interval sorting trays. Lining up data strips by length and folding them into quarters introduces medians and quartiles tangibly.
cpa.pictorial: Dot plots, frequency histograms, box-and-whisker diagrams, and scatter plots with visual trend corridors.
cpa.abstract: Five-number summary: Min, $Q_1$, $Q_2$ (Median), $Q_3$, Max. $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$. Grouped mean $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$ with class midpoints $x$.

misconceptions.description: Calculating median directly from unsorted list without ordering.
misconceptions.probe: Always sort the dataset from least to greatest before finding quartiles.

misconceptions.description: Dividing sum of the 4 midpoints by 4 without weighting by frequency counts.
misconceptions.probe: Find the midpoint ($x$) of each interval: $[50,60) \to 55$, etc.

skills.title: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square

cpa.concrete: Algebra tiles to model completing the square. Split the x bars equally into two sets, place them on adjacent sides of an x² square, and note the missing corner to see why we add (b/2)² unit tiles.
cpa.pictorial: Split-Coefficient Area Grid Boxes: square with dimension $(x + b/2)$ missing a small corner square of area $(b/2)^2$.
cpa.abstract: Completing the square: $x^2 + bx = \left(x + \frac{b}{2}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{b}{2}\right)^2$. Formula $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$. Discriminant $\Delta > 0$ (2 real roots), $\Delta = 0$ (1 repeated root), $\Delta < 0$ (no real roots).

misconceptions.description: Forgetting the $\pm$ sign when taking the square root, losing the second solution.
misconceptions.probe: Move $-2$ to the other side: $x^2 - 6x = 2$.

misconceptions.description: Evaluating $-(-3)$ as $-3$ or calculating $(-3)^2$ as $-9$ under the radical.
misconceptions.probe: Clear fractions by multiplying every term by the common denominator $x(x + 1)$.
